...HEAT ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM NOON TODAY TO 8 PM EDT THIS
EVENING...
.DISCUSSION...
Winds today will be light and variable this morning, then more 
out of the west-northwest around 5 mph late in the morning into
the afternoon. Isolated showers and storms will develop near the 
site late this afternoon after 3 PM. This could cause winds to 
become more variable, even if not over the burn itself. A weak sea
breeze may approach the site late in the afternoon, which would 
cause winds to turn more southerly. Dispersions will become good
this afternoon.
Tonight, there may be a lull in rain chances early in the evening,
followed by a weakening band of showers and storms late in the
evening after 9 PM. If this band holds together, gusty northeast
winds would be possible with the storms, or any outflow that comes
from the decaying storms. Otherwise, winds will be light out of
the west or calm through the night.
Outside of storms, dangerous heat is expected with highs in the
upper 90s and heat index values of 105-110.

WEST VIRGINIA...MARYLAND EAST OF THE ALLEGHENY FRONT...AND 
WASHINGTON DC THROUGH EARLY THIS EVENING...
Through 6 PM this evening, there is an Elevated Fire Danger which
extends across the entire eastern West Virginia Panhandle. A dry
and gusty north to northwesterly wind continues through the
afternoon with relative humidity values averaging around 20 to 25
percent. By the evening and overnight period, the influence of
robust Canadian high pressure will be felt as conditions turn much
colder. Freezing temperatures are expected tonight with low
temperatures falling into the mid/upper 20s, coupled with light
northeasterly winds. However, the dry nature of the air mass will
be felt with only moderate overnight recoveries (55 to 60 percent
relative humidity).
Once early morning temperature inversions mix out, expect ample
heating to take place as mixing heights rise to around 3,000 feet.
Given subsidence underneath the high pressure center, the depth of
mixing should be less than recent days. Winds will be on the 
lighter side while mainly being out of the northeast. Conditions 
remain dry with daytime relative humidities around 20 to 25 
percent again.
Precipitation chances remain low through the week with warming
temperatures heading toward the weekend.

morning hours and give way to mostly clear skies in the afternoon.

from 4-6 PM. 20 ft winds will be NE at 2 mph or less at ignition

15-17 mph by 10 AM and through the afternoon. These transport winds 
combined with mixing heights peaking around 6000 ft will contribute 
to good smoke dispersal and ADI values over 100 from 2 PM to 5 PM,

around sunset. In spite of mostly clear skies and light winds

site. Please feel free to contact us if you have any further 
questions or concerns.

and better rain/storm chances moving across eastern Kentucky late 
Saturday into Sunday morning.

into the area the south this morning. These clouds will likely

ft or above 1.2 KM, but gusty northwest winds between 15-20 mph,

passage from earlier in the morning. RH values could drop into

needed. Given wetting rains on Thursday, fuel moistures might be
high enough to quell more widespread fire danger.

front, which looks to bring wetting rains Sunday evening/night.

the impacts of some gusty southeasterly flow (20-30 mph gusts).

northwesterly winds overspread the area Monday evening into
Tuesday. High pressure returns by the middle of next week.
